title: Expose rendered legends to CSS selectors
body:
I've been thinking about https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/3934 in light of https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/3094, and wondering how to make that awe-inspiring exposition of fieldset/legend rendering accessible to CSS selectors. For reference, here's the [current model](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/rendering.html#rendered-legend): > If the element's box has a child box that matches the conditions in the list below, then the first such child box is the 'fieldset' element's **rendered legend**: > > The child is a `legend` element. > The child's used value of 'float' is 'none'. > The child's used value of 'position' is not 'absolute' or 'fixed'. A problem from the perspective of CSS is that this defines a _box_ as opposed to an _element_ (cf. [CSS Display](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-display-3/#intro)), and does so with reference to used values, which are unknown until almost the end of the [value processing calculation](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-cascade-4/#value-stages). In combination, this means that style application can change the identity of a rendered legend—not just between "absent" and "present", but even from one `legend` to another! It is possible to fix this, but the changes would have observable effects. I want to know if they would be web-compatible, though (and given how recently #3934 landed, I'm hoping that they are). The proposal is this: * Define a fieldset's **principal legend** (name subject to bikeshedding) as its first child legend, i.e. `fieldset > legend:first-of-type`. * Redefine a fieldset's **rendered legend** as the box associated with a non-floating non-absolute/fixed principal legend, retaining the new rendering model. * Investigate how to define the above in terms of CSS such that it could be leveraged by user agent and/or author stylesheets, particularly for _disabling_ the special default treatment of principal legends. And the most obvious effects of this proposal: * It would prevent legends with preceding legend siblings from ever generating rendered legend boxes. ```html
not a rendered legend, because floating not a rendered legend, because not the first legend
``` * It would prevent legends deeper in the element tree from _ever_ generating rendered legend boxes. ```html
not a rendered legend, because not a direct fieldset child
rendered legend
``` I highly doubt that even 0.001% of loaded pages depend upon such legends getting the magic treatment, but that's just speculation that I can't back up with data. But I do want to find out, because bringing that magic into the fold of CSS would be very nice indeed.
